Cross-Validate Conditional Choices in Complete Matched Sets

Source: R/cv_choice.R
cross_validate_clogit.Rd

Cross-validate a step-selection model or another conditional logistic model. In each fold, refit the coefficients, and optionally the scales of effect, using the analysis rows, then score the probability the model gives the used alternative among all alternatives of each held-out choice set. A choice set is one used alternative together with the available alternatives it was chosen from, for example one observed step and its random steps.

Usage

cross_validate_clogit(
  formula,
  data,
  folds,
  kernel_inputs = NULL,
  backend = c("conditional_logit", "refit"),
  method = c("exact", "efron", "breslow"),
  cox_control = survival::coxph.control(),
  optim_args = list(),
  keep_fits = FALSE,
  keep_selection = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR_choice_cv'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

formula

Two-sided formula. The response is a numeric or logical column coded 1 for the used alternative and 0 for the available ones. The right side holds the predictors and one bare strata(choice_id) term naming the column that identifies each choice set. Factors, interactions, offsets, and the data-dependent terms scale(), poly(), splines::ns(), and splines::bs() are allowed. A dot (.) expands to the columns of data, so remove the set ID from it, for example case_ ~ . - step + strata(step).

data

Data frame with one row per alternative, holding the case column, the set ID, and every predictor. Its row names are the row IDs used by folds and, when supplied, by kernel_inputs. They must be unique.

folds

Named list of explicit splits of row IDs, as in cross_validate(). Every choice set must lie wholly in the analysis rows, wholly in the assessment rows, or wholly outside the split. grouped_cv_folds() applied to the set IDs, or to animal IDs, does this. See "Build folds that keep choice sets whole".

kernel_inputs

Optional multiScaleR_data object from kernel_prep() or kernel_prep_by_group() with the cell-level data kept, one prepared row per alternative. The default NULL fits an ordinary conditional logistic reference model without scales. When it is supplied, each fold also estimates the scales, and learns the standardization and distance bins, from its analysis rows only.

backend

Scale-fitting route used with kernel_inputs, either "conditional_logit" (default) or "refit". Supply optim_args = list(radius_grid = ...) with "refit" to profile hard radii, together with any smooth scales, in each training split. The usual kernel, metric, and numerical checks of multiScale_optim() apply. Ignored when kernel_inputs is NULL.

method

Partial-likelihood method passed to survival::clogit(), one of "exact" (default), "efron", or "breslow". These are rules for tied event times. With one used alternative per set they give the same likelihood, but the method is recorded, and cv_tab() and select_cv() compare only candidates that declare the same method.

cox_control

Named list of survival::coxph.control() settings for the native training fit. The default keeps the settings of coxph.control().

optim_args

Named list of extra multiScale_optim() arguments used in every fold, such as par or profile_control. Supply radius_grid with backend = "refit" to profile hard radii, together with any smooth scales, in each training split. Supply covariate_transform = "raw" with backend = "refit" to keep optimized covariates in their own units (see "Keep optimized covariates in their own units"). Arguments that supply data, the starting model, a custom refit function, parallel workers, backend, or verbose are reserved. Every fold runs on one worker. The default list() keeps the backend's own defaults. Choose starting values without using the assessment outcomes.

keep_fits

Logical. The default FALSE keeps the predictions, scores, fold estimates, and compact diagnostics. TRUE also keeps the full fitted model of every fold in fits, which can use much more memory. You need full fits only to inspect the fold models or to have select_cv() return the selected fits.

keep_selection

Logical. TRUE keeps a compact record of each fold's training likelihood and parameter count in selection_records, which is what select_cv() needs when keep_fits = FALSE. The records come from the fits already run, so they add no fitting time. The default is FALSE.

x

A multiScaleR_choice_cv result, for print().

...

Not used. Reserved for future print controls.

Value

A list of class multiScaleR_choice_cv, which inherits from multiScaleR_cv. Its summary holds the negative log score of the used alternative, averaged over held-out choice sets, and predictions holds one row per alternative with its probability within its set. The other elements follow cross_validate(). The conditional-choice section of multiScaleR_cv lists every difference. print() shows how many folds were scored and the pooled score, and returns x invisibly.

Build folds that keep choice sets whole

Before any fitting, the function rejects a split that divides a choice set. Holding out whole choice sets measures transfer to new sets from the same animals. To measure transfer to new animals, build the folds from animal IDs instead. If step labels repeat across animals, first create a globally unique set ID, such as interaction(animal, step, drop = TRUE), and use that column in strata(). For spatial blocks, pass the set IDs or the animal IDs as group to spatial_cv_folds(), so that no set crosses a split boundary.

What the model can contain

Each set needs exactly one used alternative and at least one available alternative. Weights, missing values, robust clustering (cluster()), frailty and other special or penalized Cox terms, and general censored survival responses are outside this function, and no rows are dropped silently. Predictors that are constant within every set have no identifiable coefficient. Native alias and convergence problems are kept as failures rather than resolved by dropping terms or alternatives, and a warning from the native training fit makes the fold fail. Every scored fold checks that its native fit is unweighted and unpenalized, uses the analysis rows and complete sets, and used the declared method, whether or not fits or records are kept. Learned transformations follow the rules described in cross_validate(). Their training constants add no stratum effects and do not change the event count.

Estimate scales within the folds

With kernel_inputs, each fold rebuilds the spatial covariates from the raw cells of its analysis rows, learns the standardization and the representative bin distances there, and estimates the scales. The assessment rows reuse those frozen references. Inputs from kernel_prep_by_group() are fixed covariate maps and add no random effects. Raw covariate units (covariate_transform = "raw" in optim_args) require backend = "refit". vignette("v04-landscape-metrics", package = "multiScaleR") shows a search over a grid of radii on a full data set.

Read the scores

The score of a held-out set is the negative natural log of the probability the fitted model gives its used alternative, where the probabilities of a set's alternatives sum to 1. The pooled score averages over sets. A model without covariates or offsets gives each of k alternatives a probability of 1/k, so its score is log(k), or 1.099 for three alternatives. A useful covariate lowers the score. Scores are computed on the log scale, so a probability that prints as zero still has a finite score. Predictions use the saved training terms and assign no effect to the labels of new sets. These within-set probabilities differ from Bernoulli probabilities of use and from unnormalized relative selection strengths.

For a model with no estimated coefficients, survival's logLik() can return NA. The function then checks survival's stored null log-likelihood against the exact complete-set likelihood before using it, with K = 0, for training-criterion selection. Missing or inconsistent values remain failures. Other native fits are not altered.

Compare and select models

Use cv_tab() with metric = "neg_log_score" to rank choice models fitted to the same sets, folds, and method. Use select_cv() to score a training AIC, AICc, or BIC rule. Its sample size is the number of choice sets (one event each), and K counts the coefficients and any estimated scales and shapes. Choice scores cannot be mixed with scores from Bernoulli GLMs. They treat fitted parameters as known, so they do not integrate parameter or selection uncertainty, give intervals, or establish calibration. vignette("v08-cross-validation", package = "multiScaleR") includes a step-selection example.

See also

cross_validate(), grouped_cv_folds(), spatial_cv_folds(), cv_tab(), select_cv(), and multiScaleR_cv.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # 24 choice sets of three alternatives. The first of each set was used.
  i <- 1:72
  choices <- data.frame(step = (i - 1) %/% 3 + 1,
                        used = as.numeric(i %% 3 == 1),
                        habitat = sin(i * 1.7))
  folds <- grouped_cv_folds(choices$step, k = 3)   # whole sets held out

  models <- list(
    null = cross_validate_clogit(used ~ strata(step), choices, folds,
                                 keep_selection = TRUE),
    habitat = cross_validate_clogit(used ~ habitat + strata(step), choices,
                                    folds, keep_selection = TRUE))
  print(models$habitat)   # natural-log loss per held-out choice set

  # The null model scores log(3) = 1.099. Here habitat is unrelated to use,
  # so it does not lower the score.
  print(cv_tab(models, metric = "neg_log_score"))

  # Model picked by training AICc in each fold
  select_cv(models, criterion = "AICc")$selection$chosen
}
#> Conditional-choice CV: 3 of 3 folds scored.
#>         metric estimate       unit n_assessment n_scored weight_sum complete
#>  neg_log_score 1.126067 choice_set           24       24         24     TRUE

#>              72

#> 2  habitat    2 1.126067 0.02745496 neg_log_score choice_set           24
#>   N_scored Weight_sum Warnings
